A4 corrupt / partial persisted state (10 rows + 7 ✓, 5 ✗): in_flight rows with closed_at set / verdicts present / duplicate ids / empty id list / unknown kind → status API AND drain both fail offline.wallet_corrupt before sending ✓; applied/superseded/unknown-state corrupt rows → status API fails but drain sends+settles ✗ (breaks[0]); orphaned in_flight naming a receipt that no longer exists (superseded, no crash, nothing settled) ✓; orphan naming a receipt already settled (superseded, stale not re-presented) ✓; stale in_flight from a 'previous launch' re-presents the same id exactly once ✓; another owner's corrupt row is invisible to this owner ✓; corrupt receipt body (non-JSON claims) fails typed, not as empty wallet ✓; receipt deleted between submission and answer → apply rejects offline.receipt_unknown, journal stays in_flight, nothing else settled ✓.

implement.summary:
Defect on BASE_SHA (INFERRED from code, then VERIFIED by the new suite failing on base): apps/mobile/src/data/offlineCapabilities.ts reconcileOfflineReceipts() (L1386–1410) reads pendingOfflineReceipts() (L1319), calls client.submitReceipts(...) over the network, and only then loops settleOfflineReceipt() (L1338) per verdict. Nothing durable is written between 'request left the device' and 'verdicts recorded', so (a) a process death after the server answered but before/while settling leaves receipts `settled_at IS NULL` with no record that they were ever presented — the relaunch cannot distinguish 'never sent' from 'sent, answer lost' and has no HOLD signal; (b) verdicts for a batch were applied one row at a time, so a kill mid-loop persisted a partial batch; (c) two overlapping drains (foreground trigger + 30 s cadence) could present the same receipt ids concurrently; (d) there was no JS-side wallet status API for the app to surface a HOLD. The receipt ids/operation ids themselves were already durable and the server settles by receipt id, so the fix is a write-ahead journal around the submission, not a change to consumption.

Fix (apps/mobile/src/data/offlineWallet.ts, 522 lines, wired into the shipping path): `offline_wallet_journal (owner_key, journal_id, kind, receipt_ids JSON, state in_flight|applied|superseded, opened_at, closed_at, verdicts JSON)` installed via OFFLINE_WALLET_JOURNAL_DDL in db.ts LOCAL_MIGRATIONS. reconcileOfflineWallet(db, client, reading) — now called by syncRuntime.ts's receipt drain — (1) in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction reads pending receipts, marks any prior `in_flight` entry `superseded` (counted as `recovered`), inserts a new `in_flight` entry naming the exact receipt ids, COMMITs; (2) submits exactly those ids (idempotent: same receipt ids, same operation ids, never a new operation id, never a second ticket); (3) validates the verdict list matches the presented ids 1:1 (else offline.receipt_unknown, nothing settled), then in a second transaction settles every receipt AND closes the journal `applied` with the verdicts — atomically; existing terminal settlements are never overwritten (counted `stale`). Drains are serialized per owner in-process; owner fencing via captureDataOwnerContext/forDataOwner; guest/signed-out owners never submit. readOfflineWalletStatus() reports each pending receipt's phase (queued | presented_unanswered | held) and `hold=true` when an unanswered presentation exists — a HOLD, not a refund. Malformed journal rows throw offline.wallet_corrupt rather than reading as an empty wallet.

Harness: apps/mobile/__harness__/processDeath/walletChild.ts runs the wallet path as a real Node child on a durable SQLite file (holdOfflineGrant -> consumeOfflineAllocation -> configureSyncRuntime + triggerOutboxSync) with the existing SQL/HTTP kill switches; the suite SIGKILLs it at every step, relaunches, and asserts the same receipt id/operation id, one consumed ticket, one applied journal entry, no double submission, and that a held verdict survives relaunch until accepted.
